title: St. George's Square final design approved
subtitle: Also: conservation authority consolidation resolution, bike lane winter maintenance restored, third quarter budget adjustments, advisory committee appointments.
overview: Council approved the final design for St. George's Square {{vote:m6}}. The plan keeps flexible space for events, adds trees and a wood-framed lighting promenade, and leaves out the proposed self-cleaning washroom and gateway features for now. Surface work is expected to finish in late 2027, with final touches in early 2028. Staff will keep looking for a public washroom option.

Council also asked the province to consider the Grand River Conservation Authority's alternative to large regional consolidation of conservation authorities {{vote:m12}}. It approved third quarter capital budget adjustments {{vote:m7}}, received the external audit plan, and appointed members to three advisory committees.

The mayor announced a mayoral decision that restores winter maintenance of on-street bike lanes, funded through other budget changes. Council then shortened the 21-day amendment period so the order could take effect right away {{vote:m14}}. After closed session, the mayor reported that council gave staff direction on the chief administrative officer's year-end review, 170 Stephanie Drive and an affordable housing property acquisition.

decisions.detail: Council approved the final design for St. George's Square as set out in report 2025-548.

Council asked the province to meet with the Grand River Conservation Authority and consider its alternative proposal, called for provincial funding of the new agency without municipal levies, and widened circulation to the Association of Municipalities of Ontario and other member municipalities.
Council approved the capital project funding adjustments listed in Attachment 2 (Table 4) of the third quarter budget monitoring report.
Council appointed members to the Accessibility, Economic Development and Tourism, and Transportation advisory committees for terms ending November 2026.
Council received KPMG LLP's 2025 External Audit Plan for information as part of the consent report.

debate: Staff said the St. George's Square design responds to feedback for more trees, less concrete, heritage character and flexibility. The washroom was removed because public feedback was mixed and other cities reported operating challenges with self-cleaning units.

A delegate asked for a permanent stage funded by donors instead of temporary stages. Staff said a flat area and the wide steps give flexible options, since a permanent stage would see little day-to-day use.

Another delegate said a 24/7 public washroom is needed downtown and raised concerns about the sidewalk and stairs near the bank. Staff said the grade change requires stairs, with an accessible route nearby, and that washroom work continues in the 2026 work plan.

On public art, councillors raised whether a tribute to a children's author belongs in the square, and how other local figures might be honoured. Staff said proposals go through the Arts and Culture Advisory Committee.

On the conservation authority item, the authority's chief administrative officer said every affected conservation authority shares the concerns. Councillors worried about costs being passed to municipalities after the agency's first three years and about reserves and land held by the authority.
